reasons: Across 170 deterministic runs under equal tuning budgets, identical schedules, and the same data order, CauchyLift failed to beat tuned AdamW on any of the four predeclared workloads (W1: 7.9041 vs 7.1080; W2: 7.9336 vs 7.1427; W3: 1.9428 vs 1.9226; W4: 8.1187 vs 7.5853).

On high-dimensional neural network matrices (m, n >> 1), row and column energy dispersion makes the cotransverse complement denominator D_ij approximately uniform across entries (D_ij ≈ 2 ||G||_F^2), degenerating CauchyLift analytically and empirically into Normalized Gradient Descent without momentum.

Empirical telemetry confirms this collapse: CauchyLift's gradient-update cosine alignment (0.40–0.69), stable rank (1.12–1.36), and loss trajectories match NormalizedGD within 0.05 loss units across all models, while AdamW (coordinate adaptation) and Muon (orthogonalization) achieve substantially lower losses.

Per the Research Contract kill criteria and Phase 5 gate, failure to beat AdamW on at least three workloads under equal tuning triggers an immediate FAIL_CORE rather than an unprincipled rescue with momentum, moments, clipping, or Adam fallback.
Phase 5 completes its diagnostic mission to kill weak hypotheses cheaply; downstream scaling phases (6, 7, 8) are invalidated until the theory-repair loop reopens Phases 1 and 2.
